out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. CDI: EHS emailed CFM copy of employee health policy to review information with food employees, sign, and maintain on file for future reference.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: EHS emailed CFM copy of written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: The handwashing facility located at the back of the main kitchen area is blocked by two bulk ingredients bins, preventing access by employees for easy handwashing.
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. CDI: CFM repositioned both bulk ingredients bins to make hand sinks easily accessible to employees.

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at both handwashing sinks used by food employees in the main kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. EHS instructed CFM to place hand washing sign and hand washing sinks in the main kitchen area.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: jug of whole white milk (47F) stored on front counter (behind register).
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: EHS instructed CFM to relocate jug of whole white milk to Turbo Air 2 Dr reach in cooler (front area). Per the request of the CFM, EHS emailed CFM copy of TPHC monitoring logs and written procedures for approval by health department.

violations.title: Eggs Stored at 45F or less
violations.observation: Observed an ambient air temperature above 45F holding raw shells eggs: multiple cartons of raw shelled eggs (67F) on shelf under prep table in main kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Shell eggs that have not been treated to destroy Salmonella shall be stored in refrigerated equipment that maintains an ambient temperature of 45F or less. CDI: EHS instructed CFM to relocate cartons of raw shelled eggs to Falcon walk in refrigerator to cool back to 45F or below. Per the CFM request, EHS will email CFM TPHC monitoring logs and written procedures for approval from health department.

violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: The certified food manager could not provide a food temperature measuring device.
violations.corrective_action: A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. CDI: CFM ordered probe food thermometer online during inspection.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: two bulk ingredients bins (sugar, salt, flour, etc).
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS instructed CFM to place common food label on food removed from original container.
